editorial.tldr: This page groups arXiv papers by the shared phrase "large language models"; they do not form one developing story. They cover hallucination detection (Oct 1), a security attack on speculative decoding (Oct 6), narrative-induced sycophancy (Oct 16) and hallucinations in code translation (Oct 20).
editorial.whats_new: Oct 21 adds an arXiv survey of LLM-based materials data extraction; it is a domain application, not a development of the reliability papers above it.
editorial.why_it_matters: Each paper names a distinct failure surface: hallucination probing needs hidden-state access, speculative decoding adds a draft-model attack path, sycophancy skews user-facing answers, and code translation adds hallucinated output in migrations. Treat them as separate checks, not one trend.
editorial.take_for_builders: Do not cite these papers as corroborating each other; if you migrate code with LLMs, add a hallucination check on translated output, and judge the other papers separately.
